linkedin.title: Most news feeds are broken because they are designed to keep you scrolling, not to keep you informed.
linkedin.body:
We have all been there. You open an app to catch up on the world and end up trapped in a loop of outrage, celebrity gossip, or headlines that do not actually matter to your life. The algorithm is trying to predict what will make you click, not what will make you smarter.

True personalization should be the opposite of that. It should be about respecting your time. It should mean that when you open your feed, you see the stories that actually impact your industry, your interests, and your curiosity. It is not about silencing the world, but about filtering out the noise so you can find the signal.

At Headlinne, we are building a different approach. We use AI to understand what you care about, not just what you click on. The goal is to give you a news experience that feels like it was curated by a smart editor who knows exactly what you need to know today.
linkedin.cta: You can see how we are rethinking the daily news habit at HEADLINNE.com.

beats.caption: Webb reveals dynamic panorama of star formation, including smallest known brown dwarfs
Here is how a telescope captures hidden space objects.
beats.detail: Infrared light reveals what eyes cannot see.
beats.narration: Here is how a telescope captures hidden space objects. It uses infrared light to see through cosmic dust.

beats.caption: NASA pointed it at the star-forming region IC 348.
beats.detail: A busy nursery for young stars.
beats.narration: NASA pointed the Webb telescope at a star forming region called IC 348.

beats.caption: Astronomers were hunting for tiny brown dwarfs.
beats.detail: Objects smaller than the smallest stars.
beats.narration: Astronomers used the telescope to hunt for brown dwarfs. These are objects smaller than the smallest stars.

beats.caption: They found dwarfs twice the mass of Jupiter.
beats.detail: Extremely small for these cosmic objects.
beats.narration: They actually found brown dwarfs just twice the mass of Jupiter.

beats.caption: Stars are massive compared to these small dwarfs.
beats.narration: Stars are massive compared to these small dwarfs. The size difference is quite significant.

beats.caption: This helps us understand how stars actually form.
beats.detail: Studying the limits of star creation.
beats.narration: Finding these helps us understand the limits of how stars are created in our universe.
